goal: Rust-own the public single and batched router-selection wrappers through scalar, parallel, and warp dispatch while leaving routed MoE, route promotion, whole-archive policy, and C CUDA removal unclaimed.

semantics: produce 256 probabilities per row as sqrt(softplus(logit)); non-hash selection chooses six experts by probability plus optional bias while emitted weights use normalized unbiased probability scaled to 1.5
hash routing selects six model-map indices and falls back to hash row zero when a token is outside the available hash rows; invalid selected experts receive zero weight
select warp dispatch by default, parallel dispatch when only the warp path is disabled, and scalar dispatch when parallel dispatch is disabled

implementation.adapter_boundary: the public wrappers resolve optional cached model ranges and then launch the promoted cuda-oxide scalar, parallel, or warp kernel selected by current-C environment priority
implementation.reuse_boundary: the public family reuses the measured M14.5a and M14.5b probability, normalized-weight, tie-order, hash-mode fallback, and dispatch behavior
implementation.remaining_compute_boundary: routed MoE, remaining graph compute, whole-archive retention policy, production route promotion, and C CUDA removal remain unowned
implementation.linkage_requirement: the C-linked proof retains Rust exports and embedded kernels with --whole-archive

integration_risks: the Rust wrapper intentionally rejects zero hash rows and too-short single-token output spans before launch, hardening unsafe edge cases in the current C public boundary
